digest.component_or_area: Jira family adapter seam (Cloud + Data Center shared layer)
propositions: Jira Cloud and Data Center clients share REST v2/v3 protocol differences, PAT vs ACLI auth divergence, and accountId vs name identity models that cannot be served by a single forked adapter without creating unmaintained code duplication and private-import dependencies.

The extraction of a jira_family shared layer must consolidate three independent copies of the status/priority value maps that have already drifted (deleted key disagreement), move sanitizer and classifier symbols while parameterizing ADF/limit-coupled ones by contract, and keep location-pinned modules unmoved by dependency-inverting instead.

The Data Center transport requires https by default with allow_insecure override, never disables TLS certificate verification, reads the PAT only from environment (never committed config), and accepts operator-configured resolved-status names via reconciler.resolved_statuses to avoid misclassifying resolved issues.

Cross-imports between adapters/jira and adapters/jira_datacenter must be machine-checked as a structural boundary, with exactly one definition per shared unit (value maps, sanitizers, classifiers) and one contract per varying unit (RichTextCodec for ADF vs wiki-text, UserIdentityModel for accountId vs name).

The live acceptance criterion requires bidirectional data movement (a DC-created issue appears in the local store after inbound reconcile, and a local edit appears on the DC issue after outbound reconcile) with zero unhandled exceptions, verified against a real Jira 8.17.1 Data Center instance rather than unit assertions alone.

Operator-configured least-privilege service accounts with scoped PAT tokens, internal-CA bundle support, and documented workflows prevent credential leakage and TLS interception on self-hosted Data Center deployments served over corporate networks.
